short.q: Calculate the Mr of CaCO₃ and the number of moles in 25 g. (Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16) [3]
Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. Calculate the volume of hydrogen at r.t.p. from 2.4 g Mg (Ar = 24). [3]
short.model: Moles Mg = 0.1; mole ratio 1:1 so 0.1 mol H₂; volume = 0.1 × 24 = 2.4 dm³ (2400 cm³).

short.q: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO. Calculate the mass of MgO formed from 6 g Mg (Ar: Mg 24, O 16). [3]
short.model: Mr MgO = 40; 6 g Mg = 0.25 mol; 0.25 mol MgO = 10 g.

short.q: Calculate the mass of 3.01 × 10²³ molecules of oxygen, O₂ (O = 16). [2]
A student says '1 g of H₂ and 1 g of O₂ contain the same number of molecules'. Is this correct? Explain. [2]
short.model: No. H₂ has Mr 2 and O₂ has Mr 32, so 1 g of H₂ contains far more moles and molecules.
points: different molar masses so different number of moles
